privacy.title: Privacy notice – NoTiming
privacy.heading: Privacy notice
privacy.draft: Draft. This notice describes what the platform does today. A lawyer has not reviewed it yet, and what is in square brackets is still to be filled in by the organisation that runs the platform.
privacy.who.heading: Who runs the platform
privacy.who.body: [Name and address of the organisation that runs NoTiming] runs the platform and decides what is done with the details below. You can write to [contact email] about anything in this notice.
privacy.account.heading: What we keep about your account
privacy.account.body: We keep your email address, your name and your country and, if you give them, your club and your FEI ID. If you add a passkey we keep its public part and the name you gave it, and never a fingerprint or a face. A sign-in code we send you works for ten minutes, and you stay signed in for up to thirty days after you last used the platform. We keep the access that organisers have given you to an Event (as an Official, an Operator or a Console Operator), the Snapshots you send, which account recorded a time and when, and, if you link yourself to an Athlete or to Horses, which ones.
privacy.riders.heading: What the registries and the Results show about riders and horses
privacy.riders.body: Organisers register the Athletes, Horses and Clubs of their country and enter them in Events. A registry row holds a name, a name in English, a FEI ID, a club and a country. Anybody can see the startlist and the Results of an Event, which show names, placings and times and may show the club and the country. A signed-in account can search the registries of every country by name, and then sees the name and the name in English of an Athlete or a Horse and nothing else; the FEI ID, the club and the country of a rider are shown only to the organisers who set an Event up (a Tenant Root, the Console Operator of an Event that is not over, and the developer of the platform), because the Setup of an Event needs them. [To be confirmed: which of the club, the country and the FEI ID the public views of an Event show.] Some riders are under 18. [How their details are entered with the agreement of a parent or guardian is to be confirmed.]
privacy.why.heading: Why we keep it
privacy.why.body: To run your account, to let organisers run their Events and publish their Results, and to show the history of an Athlete or a Horse to the signed-in people who look for it. [Legal basis to be confirmed.] We do not sell these details and we do not use them for advertising.
privacy.recipients.heading: Who else receives it
privacy.recipients.body: Our email provider, Brevo, receives your email address and the text of the mails we send you. Our hosting and database providers [names to be confirmed] store the data for us. Organisers see the people they give access to and the registries of their own Events as described above. We give your details to nobody else unless the law requires it.
privacy.keep.heading: How long we keep it
privacy.keep.body: We keep an account until you ask us to delete it. The Results of an Event stay as a record of that Event. [How long, and what is deleted with an account, to be confirmed.]
privacy.cookies.heading: Cookies and the storage of your browser
privacy.cookies.body: We use only what the platform needs: a cookie that keeps you signed in, and short-lived cookies that protect sign-in, registration and passkeys from forgery. Your browser also keeps the language you chose and the Snapshots that could not be sent yet. We use no advertising or tracking cookies. [To be confirmed: any measurement of how the platform is used.]
privacy.rights.heading: Your rights
privacy.rights.body: You can ask for a copy of your details, for a correction or for deletion, and you can object to how they are used, by writing to [contact email]. You can also complain to the data protection authority of your country. [Authority and procedure to be confirmed.]
